h1: US Visa Appointment Wait Times in India: The Consulate Gap Nobody Uses

coverSpec.title: US visitor visa waits at Indian consulates ranged from about 60 to about 315 days in August 2026
coverSpec.desc: In August 2026 the interview-required B-1/B-2 wait was about 315 days at Hyderabad, about 255 days at Mumbai and New Delhi, and about 60 days at Kolkata. All five Indian posts run on the same scheduling platform under the same rules, and India has allowed only one reschedule per MRV fee since 1 January 2025, which makes the choice of post the most consequential decision an applicant makes.

faq.q: How long is the US visa appointment wait in India right now?
faq.a: It depends entirely on the consulate. In August 2026 the interview-required B-1/B-2 wait was about 315 days at Hyderabad, about 255 days at Mumbai and New Delhi, and about 60 days at Kolkata. The State Department's own published averages in late July 2026 put Mumbai at 11 months, Hyderabad at 10, New Delhi at 8 and Chennai at 7. Figures move week to week, so check the official wait time tool for your post rather than quoting any article.

faq.q: Which Indian consulate has the shortest US visa wait?
faq.a: Kolkata has consistently been the shortest of the Indian posts, and in August 2026 it was around 60 days for interview-required visitor visas against roughly 315 at Hyderabad. It is also the post applicants think about least, which is part of why it stays shorter. Whether you can use it depends on the consular district rules that apply to your application, so check before you plan around it.

faq.q: How many times can I reschedule a US visa appointment in India?
faq.a: Once per MRV fee, and that has been the position since 1 January 2025. It is one of the tightest allowances in the world: several countries allow three and some allow six. The practical effect is that an Indian applicant cannot iterate towards a better date. You get one move, so it has to be the right one, and using it on a small improvement is how people end up stuck.

faq.q: Can I apply for a US visa in Dubai or Canada instead of India?
faq.a: Not usefully any more. Since the State Department's guidance of 6 September 2025, updated on 10 October 2025, applicants are directed to schedule in their country of nationality or legal residence, and those who apply elsewhere are told they may find it more difficult to qualify. Fees are neither refunded nor transferred if it goes wrong. The UAE and Canada were the two most popular third country routes for Indian applicants, which is exactly why the guidance closed them.

faq.q: Why is the wait so different between Indian consulates?
faq.a: Because a wait time is staffing divided by demand, and both vary. Hyderabad serves a region with unusually heavy petition-based and student traffic, which competes for the same interview capacity as visitor cases. Kolkata's catchment is smaller and its visitor demand lighter. Nothing about the rules or the portal differs between them, which is what makes the gap usable if your consular district allows it.

faq.q: Are student visa waits in India shorter than visitor visa waits?
faq.a: Substantially, and deliberately so. In August 2026 the F, M and J wait was around 75 days at Mumbai and New Delhi against 255 days for visitor visas, and petition-based H, L, O, P and Q cases were shorter still at around 45 days. Consular sections prioritise students and workers against fixed start dates. If you are in one of those categories, the visitor visa headline numbers are not your queue.

faq.q: Do these wait times include administrative processing?
faq.a: No, and this catches people out badly. The published figure measures how far away the next interview appointment is, and nothing else. If your case goes into administrative processing after the interview, that time is additional, unpredictable and outside anyone's control. Plan the interview date with these numbers and leave real margin after it before any non-refundable travel.

cta.heading: One reschedule attempt is a decision, not a habit
cta.body: That is what makes India different from almost everywhere else. If your country allowed six attempts you could experiment, and you cannot. Spending your single move on a two week improvement, and then finding a four month one two days later, is the most common and most expensive mistake Indian applicants make. If you would rather that judgement was somebody's job, tell us your post, your current date and the widest range you could accept, and we will tell you honestly whether it is worth paying us at all.
